patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient presents with a complaint of severe vulvar itching that has been gradually worsening over the course of the past year. She has attempted to use over-the-counter lubricants for relief with no substantial improvement. She reports severe pain during vaginal intercourse that has recently led to cessation of sexual activity.

Secondary_Symptoms: Use of over-the-counter lubricants with no relief

patient_actor_hidden.Past_Medical_History: Diet-controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension treated with hydrochlorothiazide, menopause occurred at 52 years of age.
patient_actor_hidden.Social_History: Sexually active with her husband until recently due to discomfort.
patient_actor_hidden.Review_of_Systems: Denies urinary symptoms, abnormal vaginal discharge, or rectal symptoms.

objective_for_doctor: Evaluate and diagnose the patient presenting with chronic vulvar itching and discomfort.

turns.doctor_opening: Hello, what brings you in today? Could you tell me about yourself and what's been going on?
turns.patient_opening: “Well, over the past year my vulva has been extremely itchy, and it’s been gradually getting worse. I’ve tried over-the-counter lubricants, but they haven’t helped much, and sex has become very painful so I’ve stopped.”

turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any changes in my vision—no blurriness, dark spots, or loss of vision. My main issue has been the severe vulvar itching that’s been worsening over the past year and the pain with intercourse.”
